drs_observed.explanation: England's 2011 'NatWest Series' is two bilateral series under one name: England v Sri Lanka (5 ODIs, no reviews recorded) and England v India (DRS without ball-tracking; reviews in 2 of 5). The series key splits NatWest Series by team pair from 2006, so per-match drs_available is right; only this event-level row pools them.

The 2025 Zimbabwe T20I tri-series in Harare (Zimbabwe, New Zealand, South Africa) had no DRS, while the Pakistan tri-series with Zimbabwe did. The default is per team, so New Zealand v South Africa in Harare stays 'all'; per-match drs_available is false there through the series key.

pooled.explanation: Australia show three failed fielding reviews before over 80 of the West Indies second innings at Melbourne (match 892517); the allowance was two. Likely a mis-attributed or untagged review.
Australia show three failed fielding reviews before over 80 at Dhaka (match 1104284), a month before umpire's-call retention; likely a mis-attributed review.

overs_balls.explanation: Cricsheet info.overs is 50 for 12 men's T20Is that have 20-over innings; 3 innings credit one bowler with 5 overs (attribution errors).
Cricsheet info.overs is 50 for 7 women's T20Is that have 20-over innings; 3 innings credit one bowler with 5 overs (attribution errors).

replacements.explanation: A single supersub-coded replacement in WBBL 2020/21; WBBL did not use the BBL X-factor rule, so it is treated as a non-tactical replacement.

super_overs.explanation: The 2020 quarter-final Leicestershire v Nottinghamshire (match 1207789) is recorded as a tie with no super over.
One 2021/22 group match (1299613) went to a super over; the other CSA T20 group ties stood.
Bangladesh v India women, 2023-07-22 (1382168): tie with no super over played.
Scotland v Ireland in the 2018 Netherlands tri-series (1142504): tie with no super over.

min_overs_for_result.explanation: Marsh Cup match 1322388 records a 19.5-over D/L target; the chase was set for 20 overs less one ball, treated as the 20-over minimum.

reduced_powerplays.explanation: Two 19-over BBL matches (1152515, 1152565) record a 5-over powerplay in both innings, where round_half_up(0.3 x 19) gives 6: rounding down, as in the earliest T20 seasons (IPL 2008, T20Is 2007). Other BBL seasons round half up.
The 2014 One-Day Cup mixes rounding: where floor and round_half_up of N/5 differ, 4 innings round down and 5 round half up; the rest of the unmatched innings were cut during the powerplay.
One 48-over women's ODI (1168164) records a 9-over powerplay in both innings (floor of 48/5) instead of 10.
The first WBBL power-surge season records 2-over powerplays for 12- and 13-over innings (1323574, 1323594) where ceil(N/5) gives 3; later WBBL and BBL seasons follow max(2, ceil(N/5)).

The Hundred's reduced powerplay rests on 13 scored innings and no published table: 25-80-ball innings follow round_half_up(B/4) (9 of 9), but 85- and 90-ball innings record 20 balls (3 innings) and one 65-ball chase 15. Low confidence.
